value.body: A drilling engineer plans how an oil or gas well will be drilled — depths, casing, drilling fluids, equipment — and then helps supervise the work on the rig. Upstream oil and gas companies, drilling contractors and oilfield service firms hire them. Field days follow the rig's round-the-clock operations; office days go into well planning, cost tracking and reports.

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Rotational field duty on onshore or offshore rigs

items.label: Wells drilled by ONGC
items.note: 109 exploratory and 469 development wells; 544 in FY2023-24
items.source: ONGC results / Ministry of Petroleum (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join upstream PSUs as trainee or assistant engineers, usually through GATE or the company's own exam followed by interviews, or join drilling contractors and service companies through campus hiring. Freshers often start in rig-site roles before moving to planning.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Well planning and casing design basics
Reading daily drilling reports and logs
Working safely in a rig crew

value.title: At a glance
items: Hiring rises and falls with oil prices and exploration budgets.
Field rotations mean long stretches away from home, sometimes offshore or abroad.
Common next roles: senior drilling engineer, drilling superintendent, well engineering lead.
